title: Implement CI pipeline for format, lint, unit, integration, and e2e tests
description: Configure CI to run Cargo formatting/lints/unit tests, fixture-backed integration tests, containerized package-manager e2e suites, and the secret/repository invariant gates.
acceptance_criteria: Required checks run from a clean checkout with cached but reproducible dependencies, produce useful failure artifacts, and gate merges.

title: Automate build, quality, supply-chain, and release gates
description: As a maintainer, I need reproducible CI that prevents formatting, lint, test, dependency, artifact, and container regressions from reaching releases.
acceptance_criteria: A clean checkout runs enforced formatting/lints/tests/security checks and builds the release/container artifacts; release provenance and versioning are documented.

title: Create minimal valid package and OCI artifact fixtures
description: Produce or source redistributable minimal wheels/sdists, RPMs, DEBs, pacman packages/databases/signatures, and their agreed OCI manifests/metadata alongside malformed variants.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures are reproducible, small, licensed/documented, validate against the artifact schema, and include missing/blob-mismatch/bad-metadata cases.

title: Implement programmable GHCR-compatible registry test server
description: Build a local test registry or harness with OCI v2 manifest/blob behavior, configurable public/private repositories, `WWW-Authenticate` challenges, expected request assertions, ranges, cache validators, faults, and large streams.
acceptance_criteria: Tests can declare expected method/path/headers and responses; fixture supports all required success/failure/auth/range scenarios without external network access.

title: Build a GHCR-compatible OCI registry fixture and artifact corpus
description: As a maintainer, I need deterministic public/private OCI registry fixtures and valid package artifacts so every protocol adapter is tested without relying on live GitHub Packages.
acceptance_criteria: The fixture serves manifests/blobs, auth/token challenges, failures, and controlled observability; the corpus includes valid and invalid artifacts for each approved ecosystem.

title: Add automated log/error/telemetry secret-redaction checks
description: Capture logs, errors, metrics, and traces for successful and failed authenticated requests and scan for authorization data, token fragments, signed URLs, or bodies.
acceptance_criteria: A CI check fails when known secret canaries appear in emitted telemetry; diagnostics retain sufficient sanitized correlation information.

title: Create exact OCI repository-name invariant tests
description: Exercise every frontend request shape and assert the outbound OCI `/v2/<repository>/…` path contains exactly the contract-selected repository string, with no case/namespace/prefix/fallback alteration.
acceptance_criteria: Parameterized tests cover positive names plus invalid paths and show no cross-repository request can be induced by package metadata or URL tampering.

title: Test SSRF, traversal, header injection, and redirect defenses
description: Attack the inbound and OCI boundaries with traversal, percent-encoding ambiguity, hostile metadata URLs, control characters, hop-by-hop headers, oversized inputs, redirect responses, and alternate hosts.
acceptance_criteria: Every vector fails before unsafe upstream access or follows the explicit allowlist policy; regression tests prove no credential can cross the allowed upstream boundary.

title: Create cross-protocol credential forwarding and challenge tests
description: For PyPI, RPM, APT, and pacman flows, test anonymous, Basic, and Bearer-compatible requests plus GHCR-style `WWW-Authenticate`, 401, and 403 exchanges using a controlled registry fixture.
acceptance_criteria: Tests assert equivalent incoming authorization is sent only upstream, client-visible status/challenges are correct, proxy-owned credentials are never substituted, and no Authorization value appears in artifacts.

title: Verify credential transparency and exact repository isolation
description: As a security-conscious registry user, I need proof that the proxy forwards my registry credentials only to the configured GHCR-compatible upstream and never rewrites or escapes the repository I requested.
acceptance_criteria: Automated tests cover every protocol and prove auth/challenge relay, credential redaction, exact repository selection, no cross-repository blob access, and upstream-boundary hardening.

title: Validate cross-protocol security, conformance, and release readiness
description: Establish reusable registry fixtures, security regression gates, performance bounds, CI checks, operational documentation, and release criteria for the Rust package-protocol proxy.
acceptance_criteria: All selected frontends have end-to-end evidence, credential/repository invariants pass, automated quality gates are enforced, operator/client docs are published, and a production release checklist is approved.

title: Relay GHCR authentication headers and challenges transparently
description: Forward permitted caller authorization to only the configured registry and faithfully return upstream `WWW-Authenticate`, 401, and 403 semantics without logging or replacing credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Fake GHCR token-challenge tests prove forwarding, challenge relay, anonymous behavior, host isolation, and credential redaction.

title: Implement OCI manifest and blob retrieval operations
description: Implement typed requests for `/v2/<repository>/manifests/<reference>` and `/v2/<repository>/blobs/<digest>`, including HEAD where the contract needs it and descriptor parsing.
acceptance_criteria: A registry fixture confirms GET/HEAD method, encoded reference/digest behavior, accepted media types, descriptor parsing, and streamed blob retrieval.

title: Enforce exact OCI repository-name use in gateway URLs
description: Make repository selection an opaque validated value from the mapping contract and prohibit gateway helpers from changing case, namespace, separators, prefixes, or fallback targets.
acceptance_criteria: Tests assert outbound `/v2/` paths retain the chosen repository string exactly for every supported adapter context and reject cross-repository attempts.

title: Implement authenticated OCI Distribution API gateway
description: As a frontend adapter, I need a reusable client for GHCR-compatible manifest and blob retrieval that sends the caller's credentials and preserves the exact requested repository name.
acceptance_criteria: The gateway constructs verified OCI v2 requests, performs media-type negotiation, streams blobs, relays auth challenges, and has integration tests asserting method/path/header correctness.

title: Implement backpressured upstream request and response streaming
description: Build the async body bridge so large responses move between client and registry with backpressure, no disk spill, and cancellation when either peer disconnects.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-gigabyte-equivalent generated stream demonstrates bounded memory, cancellation releases resources, and body errors are surfaced safely.

title: Preserve approved HTTP headers, cache validators, and ranges
description: Implement a narrow header policy retaining Content-Type, Content-Length, ETag, Last-Modified, Cache-Control, Range, Content-Range, and Accept-Ranges as specified; remove hop-by-hop and unsafe headers.
acceptance_criteria: Tests verify correct request/response range and conditional behavior, header filtering, and no forwarding of connection-specific or sensitive proxy headers.

title: Provide low-memory streaming HTTP transport
description: As a package client, I need archives and metadata to pass through without whole-body buffering while retaining required HTTP semantics.
acceptance_criteria: The transport streams request/response bodies with bounded memory, preserves the approved headers/status/range behavior, and handles timeout/cancellation safely.

title: Enforce inbound path, header, and request-size limits
description: Apply the security contract at the proxy edge: method allowlists, normalized path validation without traversal, header count/size controls, and bounded request bodies.
acceptance_criteria: Negative tests prove malformed paths, control characters, oversized headers/bodies, and unsupported methods fail before any upstream request.

title: Implement protocol-aware inbound routing and safe errors
description: As an adapter developer, I need one typed routing boundary that identifies a frontend, extracts only validated request context, and returns consistent non-leaking errors.
acceptance_criteria: Routing dispatches configured protocol routes deterministically, rejects ambiguous/malformed paths before upstream access, and returns documented method/not-found/validation errors.

title: Create frontend route dispatcher and validated request context
description: Implement a router that assigns incoming paths to PyPI, RPM, APT, or pacman adapters based on explicit configuration and produces typed, validated context without deciding OCI repository names prematurely.
acceptance_criteria: Route unit tests cover method/path matching, conflicting routes, percent-encoding, trailing-slash behavior, and disabled frontends.

title: Implement validated runtime configuration with secure defaults
description: Implement configuration for listen address, GHCR upstream URL, allowed host(s), timeouts, header/body limits, log level, and explicit frontend enablement; fail fast for unsafe values.
acceptance_criteria: Configuration accepts documented env/file inputs, rejects unsafe upstreams and invalid limits, and tests default/override/error cases.

title: Bootstrap Cargo workspace and pinned minimal HTTP stack
description: Create the Rust workspace, choose an async HTTP stack that supports streaming, set MSRV/toolchain policy, enable lint/format/test commands, and keep dependencies justified for a low-CPU proxy.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test` run in a fresh checkout; the dependency and MSRV decisions are documented.

title: Build Rust proxy foundation and transparent OCI/GHCR gateway
description: Implement the low-memory Rust HTTP service, typed routing, streamed upstream transport, and reusable OCI Distribution API gateway required by every package frontend.
acceptance_criteria: The service safely starts, routes protocol requests, streams bodies, preserves approved HTTP semantics, performs exact-name authenticated OCI retrieval, and passes core integration tests.

title: Create minimal Rust service skeleton and runtime configuration
description: As an operator, I need a small, deterministic service with validated configuration, health checks, graceful shutdown, and safe defaults.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible Rust build exposes documented configuration, liveness/readiness endpoints, graceful termination, and redacted structured logs with no package frontend behavior assumed.

title: Document upstream-boundary threat model and controls
description: Threat-model SSRF, path/header injection, redirects, credential disclosure, response smuggling, decompression/size abuse, and cross-repository blob access; select concrete mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: Threat model assigns mitigations and verification tests for every identified risk, including TLS verification, host allowlisting, redirects disabled or allowlisted, and request limits.

title: Specify credential forwarding and OCI challenge relay
description: Define supported incoming Authorization forms, forwarding rules, handling of `WWW-Authenticate`, bearer-token challenges, anonymous requests, and status propagation for GHCR-compatible registries.
acceptance_criteria: A sequence diagram and normative rules show credentials are forwarded only to the allowlisted registry and 401/403/challenges reach clients without proxy substitution.

title: Define transparent authentication and upstream security contract
description: As a GitHub Packages user, I need the proxy to preserve registry authorization semantics while preventing credentials or arbitrary upstream targets from escaping the request boundary.
acceptance_criteria: The contract defines auth forwarding/challenge relay, redaction, TLS/host/redirect/header controls, resource limits, anonymous behavior, and testable security invariants.

title: Design versioned OCI artifact layout and metadata schema
description: Specify how repository indexes, protocol metadata, packages, signatures, layer descriptors, annotations, media types, checksums, and architecture/release dimensions are represented in OCI.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned schema with manifest/layer examples supports every approved frontend and enables immutable blob retrieval by digest.

title: Define immutable request-to-OCI artifact mapping
description: As a package consumer, I need incoming requests to select the backing OCI repository without name rewriting and package metadata/files to resolve deterministically to OCI manifests and blobs.
acceptance_criteria: The contract defines repository extraction per frontend, an exact-name invariant, OCI tags/digests/media types/annotations, metadata generation rules, and protocol-specific missing-artifact errors.

title: Specify exact backing-repository selection invariant
description: For every frontend route, define the path/config component that names the backing repository. It must be used in upstream `/v2/<repository>/…` requests unchanged: no prefixing, namespace insertion, fallback, case transformation, or aliasing.
acceptance_criteria: Examples for every supported protocol show input requests and byte-for-byte identical selected OCI repository strings; invalid registry names have documented rejection behavior.

title: Specify supported package-client protocol variants
description: Document exact client and protocol targets: PyPI Simple API representation; RPM client/metadata scope; APT suite/component/architecture/signing behavior; and pacman database/signature scope.
acceptance_criteria: A compatibility matrix maps each selected client operation to HTTP routes, required metadata, status/error semantics, and minimum tested versions.

title: Confirm initial scope: four named package types
description:
## Decision
The initial release supports exactly four package types: PyPI, RPM, Debian/APT, and Arch/pacman. No fifth protocol is required or implied.

## Rationale
The project owner confirmed that “five” in the prompt was a typographical error. Limiting scope to the four named ecosystems makes the compatibility and OCI artifact contracts testable.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Infer an unstated fifth ecosystem: rejected; the owner confirmed none is required.
2. Count YUM/DNF separately from RPM: rejected; they are RPM repository clients/protocol variants, not an additional package type.
3. Count APT separately from Debian: rejected; APT is the client/protocol for Debian packages, not an additional package type.
acceptance_criteria: The project plan explicitly names PyPI, RPM, Debian/APT, and Arch/pacman as the four supported package types, contains no fifth-protocol requirement, and the compatibility-matrix work may proceed.
close_reason: Resolved: the project owner confirmed that “five” was a typo; initial scope is the four named package types.

title: Define supported package protocols and OCI artifact contract
description: Establish the compatibility boundary, package-type count, immutable request-to-OCI mapping, and credential behavior before frontend implementation begins.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed, versioned contract covers every supported protocol, the repository-name invariant, OCI layout, and authentication/error behavior; all child stories are complete.

title: Resolve package scope and client compatibility matrix
description: As a maintainer, I need an explicit, testable compatibility matrix for the four approved package types—PyPI, RPM, Debian/APT, and Arch/pacman—covering clients, versions, endpoints, and non-goals so that implementation does not assume undocumented behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The roadmap names PyPI, RPM, Debian/APT, and Arch/pacman as the four supported package types; it records protocol/client versions, endpoint sets, explicit exclusions, and representative client commands.

title: Create first-release security and compatibility checklist
description: Create a reviewable checklist requiring scope decision closure, artifact contract approval, gateway/auth invariant tests, frontend conformance, signature policy approval, resource evidence, docs, and CI artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: The checklist names objective evidence/links for every criterion and blocks release on unresolved P0/P1 risk decisions.

title: Define production release criteria and operational handoff
description: As a project owner, I need a repeatable decision gate before declaring the proxy safe for production package distribution.
acceptance_criteria: A release checklist connects required security, conformance, performance, documentation, versioning, rollback, and support evidence, and is completed for the first release.

title: Write architecture and OCI artifact contract documentation
description: Publish the request flow, immutable repository-name/auth invariants, OCI layout/schema/media types, versioning/migration policy, and rationale for the resolved package scope.
acceptance_criteria: Docs include validated concrete manifest/index examples for each supported frontend and link to the formal decision records.

title: Automate reproducible binary and container release builds
description: Create a release workflow producing versioned Rust binaries/container images with non-root runtime configuration, SBOM/provenance where selected, and checksum/signature policy.
acceptance_criteria: A tagged dry run produces documented artifacts with version, checksums, container metadata, and repeatable build instructions.

title: Add Rust dependency, license, and vulnerability review automation
description: Select and configure maintained tools/policies for dependency updates, vulnerability advisories, license review, lockfile integrity, and minimal dependency surface.
acceptance_criteria: CI detects policy violations and documentation names the tools, exceptions process, and supported Rust toolchain/update cadence.

title: Run concurrency, cancellation, timeout, and upstream-fault soak tests
description: Exercise connection reuse, slow clients, client disconnects, rate-limited/timeouting registries, retries, and prolonged mixed protocol traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Soak tests detect resource leaks/deadlocks, report limits, and verify graceful shutdown plus recovery after controlled upstream faults.

title: Build streaming memory and throughput benchmark suite
description: Measure large package/blob streaming, metadata fan-out, cache validators, ranges, and concurrent downloads using deterministic generated data and record peak RSS/allocation/throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark output shows bounded memory independent of response size within a documented tolerance and retains results suitable for CI/nightly comparison.

title: Measure lightweight resource use and resilience under load
description: As an operator, I need evidence that the proxy streams efficiently and survives expected concurrent package-manager traffic without high CPU or memory consumption.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks and soak tests establish documented CPU/memory/concurrency/latency budgets for representative metadata and archive transfers, with regression thresholds where practical.

title: Add malformed metadata, integrity, and interrupted-transfer regression tests
description: Test incomplete and malformed indexes, deleted manifests/blobs, altered digests/lengths, invalid signatures, unexpected media types, partial/range responses, client cancellation, and concurrent downloads.
acceptance_criteria: Tests demonstrate safe source-protocol errors, no unbounded buffering/panics, cleanup after cancellation, and no access outside descriptor-bound artifacts.

title: Run protocol conformance and regression suites
description: As a maintainer, I can detect adapter regressions with real package-manager commands and focused malformed/partial-transfer cases.
acceptance_criteria: CI exercises each approved client’s discovery/sync/install path and protocol-safe errors with controlled OCI artifacts, and keeps a regression matrix by frontend.

title: Define executable end-to-end client conformance matrix
description: Turn the compatibility matrix into version-pinned containerized test commands for pip, approved RPM client(s), apt, and pacman, covering authenticated and anonymous repositories.
acceptance_criteria: Every claimed client operation maps to an automated command, fixture, expected result, and documented platform/container image.

title: Provide fixture publishing and test-environment setup tools
description: Provide scripts or Rust helpers to seed the test registry, create users/tokens, configure the proxy, clean isolation state, and display sanitized failures for local/CI runs.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh environment can start fixtures and execute one documented protocol smoke test with a single command; cleanup is deterministic.

title: Add authenticated pacman synchronize and install tests
description: Exercise `pacman -Sy` and `pacman -S` against public/private GHCR-compatible fixtures, including signatures, missing archives, and failed authorization.
acceptance_criteria: CI runs documented pacman flows and asserts command outcome, exact OCI repository path, credential challenge relay, and absence of leaked credentials.

title: Stream Arch archives and detached signatures
description: Stream `.pkg.tar.*` and, where selected, `.sig` OCI blobs with accurate length/cache/range behavior and descriptor agreement checks.
acceptance_criteria: Large archive fixtures demonstrate bounded memory and pacman-compatible download behavior; descriptor mismatch fails safely.

title: Bind pacman archive routes to validated OCI blobs
description: Map package archive and optional detached signature names from sync metadata to immutable descriptor-bound routes with no arbitrary blob lookup.
acceptance_criteria: All advertised archive/signature routes resolve; manipulated names, traversal, and cross-repository requests are rejected before OCI access.

title: Serve Arch package archives from immutable OCI blobs
description: As a pacman user, I can download package archives and selected detached signatures referenced by the synchronized database.
acceptance_criteria: Archive routes bind to validated OCI descriptors, stream without buffering, maintain package integrity expectations, and work against authorized registry fixtures.

title: Deliver pacman sync artifacts preserving selected signature policy
description: Pass through signed compatible database artifacts where possible, or implement the approved generation/signing model; preserve content length, caches, and safe error semantics.
acceptance_criteria: pacman accepts valid DB/signature artifacts in integration fixtures; absent/invalid signatures follow the documented policy.

title: Resolve and validate pacman OCI artifact descriptors
description: Use the shared OCI layout to resolve sync DB, files DB, and signature descriptors; validate expected media types, immutable digests, filenames, and release dimensions.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture coverage rejects absent or inconsistent descriptors and proves selected OCI repository paths are exact and unchanged.

title: Serve pacman sync databases and signatures from OCI
description: As a pacman user, I can synchronize a configured repository and retrieve compatible `.db`, optional `.files`, and signature artifacts from OCI-backed storage.
acceptance_criteria: The selected pacman database/version/architecture/signature behavior is documented and `pacman -Sy` succeeds using OCI artifacts without repository-name rewriting.

title: Implement pacman database, files, and signature routes
description: Route configured repository database names, optional `.files`, and `.sig` artifacts with strict filename and architecture validation.
acceptance_criteria: Route tests cover valid/invalid database paths, optional artifacts, signatures, architecture variants, methods, and traversal attempts.

title: Implement OCI-backed Arch/pacman repository frontend
description: Provide pacman-compatible sync databases, optional signatures/files databases, and package archive delivery from immutable OCI artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Supported pacman clients synchronize and install/update from the proxy under the documented architecture and signing policy, including transparent registry authorization.

title: Add authenticated apt update, install, and upgrade tests
description: Exercise public/private GHCR-like registry scenarios with apt update/install/upgrade, signature policy, cache refresh, missing packages, and interrupted downloads.
acceptance_criteria: CI executes the documented apt commands and checks exact OCI path/auth behavior plus client-visible results for positive and negative cases.

title: Stream .deb blobs and enforce Packages checksum agreement
description: Deliver `.deb` files from immutable OCI blobs while preserving necessary HTTP semantics and comparing descriptor information to Packages fields.
acceptance_criteria: Valid archives stream bounded-memory and apt accepts their advertised checksums; descriptor/index mismatch returns a safe failure.

title: Map APT pool paths to bound OCI blob descriptors
description: Map package `Filename` values to descriptor-bound `pool/` routes without using untrusted paths as upstream locations or permitting cross-repository blob selection.
acceptance_criteria: Tampering, traversal, malformed Filename, and cross-repository tests fail before upstream retrieval; all advertised pool paths resolve correctly.

title: Implement decided APT repository signing policy
description: Deliver the signed repository policy: OCI-carried pre-signed artifacts, controlled proxy signing/key management, or a clearly enforced development-only non-verifying mode.
acceptance_criteria: Supported apt verification succeeds with documented trusted keys; signature failure/missing-key behavior has negative tests and unsafe mode requires explicit opt-in.

title: Serve Debian package files from immutable OCI blobs
description: As an APT user, I can install a `.deb` referenced by Packages metadata from a safe immutable proxy route.
acceptance_criteria: Each package Filename resolves only to its validated OCI blob and correct size/checksum/caching/range behavior enables authenticated installs and upgrades.

title: Generate or pass through APT Release and Packages artifacts
description: Implement the approved OCI layout behavior for Release/InRelease/Packages content, compression, fields, hashes, and archive URLs, including stable deterministic rendering where generated.
acceptance_criteria: apt parses rendered/passed-through metadata and verification fixtures confirm Release checksums match every served Packages artifact.

title: Parse OCI APT metadata and package descriptor model
description: Retrieve and validate OCI descriptors for APT release/index artifacts, including package Filename, Size, SHA checksums, architecture, component, and compression metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid metadata including duplicate/conflicting package entries, missing descriptors, checksum mismatch, and cross-repository locations fails safely.

title: Implement APT dists release, index, and signature routes
description: Route `dists/<suite>/InRelease`, `Release`, `Release.gpg`, and selected `Packages[.<compression>]` variants using strict path parsing and configuration-derived distribution dimensions.
acceptance_criteria: Route tests cover suites/components/architectures/compression, disabled variants, encoded paths, traversal rejection, and deterministic repository context.

title: Serve APT release metadata and package indexes from OCI
description: As an APT user, I can run `apt update` and retrieve valid Release/InRelease/signature and Packages index artifacts from the proxy.
acceptance_criteria: The selected suite/component/architecture/compression matrix, index contents, checksums, caching, and signing policy are valid for supported apt clients.

title: Add authenticated DNF/YUM install and update tests
description: Run repository refresh and install/update paths against a GHCR-compatible fixture for both authorized and unauthorized users, including missing/corrupted archive cases.
acceptance_criteria: CI runs selected DNF/YUM commands and asserts client result, transparent auth challenge behavior, exact OCI repository path, and no credential leakage.

title: Implement OCI-backed Debian/APT repository frontend
description: Provide the selected APT release/index/signature routes and `.deb` archive delivery from immutable OCI artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Supported apt clients complete `apt update` and package installation for the documented suite/component/architecture layout with correct checksums and signing policy.

title: Stream RPM archives and validate advertised checksums
description: Stream descriptor-bound RPM blobs with length/range behavior and validate agreement between repodata checksums/sizes and OCI artifact descriptors.
acceptance_criteria: Package downloads are bounded-memory and DNF/YUM reject neither HTTP nor checksum metadata for valid fixtures; mismatch fixtures fail safely.

title: Bind RPM package locations to validated OCI descriptors
description: Map metadata `location` values to opaque/protocol-safe download routes that cannot be modified to access arbitrary blobs or repositories.
acceptance_criteria: Positive and negative tests prove every advertised RPM resolves and altered paths, cross-repo requests, or unknown descriptors fail before OCI blob access.

title: Serve RPM archives from immutable OCI blobs
description: As an RPM client, I can retrieve RPM packages referenced in repository metadata through safe, streaming proxy routes.
acceptance_criteria: Archive locations bind to validated OCI descriptors, have matching checksums/sizes, preserve relevant HTTP behavior, and work for authenticated installs.

title: Implement decided RPM metadata signing behavior
description: Deliver the scope decision for repodata signatures: validated pre-signed metadata, proxy-generated signing with key operations, or explicit unsupported behavior enforced at configuration time.
acceptance_criteria: Client signature behavior matches documented policy; invalid/missing signature conditions are deterministic and covered by fixtures.

title: Parse OCI RPM repository/index metadata into validated model
description: Fetch and validate the OCI representation for RPM repository indexes, descriptors, package locations, checksums, compression, and generation timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures reject missing descriptors, invalid checksums, inconsistent locations, or cross-repository references and produce a typed metadata model.

title: Generate or pass through valid repomd.xml and referenced metadata
description: Implement the selected artifact convention for `repomd.xml`, primary/filelists/other metadata, compression, and checksum/size fields while retaining immutable archive references.
acceptance_criteria: DNF/YUM validate repository metadata; generated/passed-through documents contain consistent checksums, sizes, locations, and safe XML encoding.

title: Implement DNF/YUM repodata route handling
description: Route `repodata/repomd.xml` and the metadata paths it references, including agreed architecture/release dimensions, without ambiguous path interpretation.
acceptance_criteria: Route tests cover all approved metadata files, methods, encoding, traversal rejection, and deterministic repository selection.

title: Serve RPM repository metadata from OCI artifacts
description: As a DNF/YUM user, I can fetch repodata rooted at `repomd.xml` that faithfully describes OCI-backed RPM archives.
acceptance_criteria: The approved metadata set, compression, checksum/timestamp semantics, and signing policy are implemented and a supported client refresh succeeds.

title: Implement OCI-backed RPM repository frontend
description: Provide selected YUM/DNF-compatible repository metadata and RPM archive delivery from the agreed OCI artifact layout.
acceptance_criteria: Supported RPM clients refresh metadata and install/update packages through the proxy with accurate repository checksums, credentials, and archive delivery.

title: Add authenticated pip install integration coverage
description: Use a GHCR-compatible fixture and representative wheel/sdist artifacts to test public/private discovery, token challenge, hashes, successful installation, missing files, and interrupted downloads.
acceptance_criteria: CI runs pip discovery/install tests against the proxy and verifies registry authorization headers, exact repository paths, and package installation outcomes.

title: Stream PyPI wheels and sdists with integrity checks
description: Use the OCI gateway to retrieve the descriptor-bound blob with appropriate media type, content length, ETag, range behavior, and supported digest verification.
acceptance_criteria: Wheel and sdist fixtures stream without buffering, preserve range/caching behavior, and fail closed on descriptor mismatch.

title: Create opaque PyPI distribution download routes
description: Design routes/tokens that bind a generated file link to the repository, artifact layout version, and immutable descriptor; reject user-supplied arbitrary manifests, registry URLs, and blob paths.
acceptance_criteria: Tampering tests cannot retrieve unadvertised blobs, cross repository boundaries, or override the configured upstream; valid links resolve to one descriptor.

title: Serve PyPI distribution files from immutable OCI blobs
description: As a pip user, I can download the wheel or source distribution selected from a Simple API page through a safe artifact route.
acceptance_criteria: Distribution URLs resolve only to descriptors advertised by the validated PyPI metadata and stream correct content, length, hash, range, authentication, and error semantics.

title: Render standards-compatible PyPI Simple API responses
description: Generate the selected HTML and/or JSON Simple API response with package-file links and required metadata, secure hash fragments, MIME/cache headers, and properly escaped untrusted values.
acceptance_criteria: Golden tests conform to the selected Simple API contract and pip accepts valid discovery responses without HTML/URL injection paths.

title: Parse and validate PyPI OCI index metadata
description: Retrieve the agreed OCI index representation and validate project names, filenames, versions, layer descriptors, hashes, yanked markers, and Requires-Python fields before rendering.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed, conflicting, or cross-repository metadata fails safely; valid fixtures produce a typed package/project model with immutable blob references.

title: Implement PyPI Simple API routes and project lookup rules
description: Route `/simple/` and `/simple/<project>/` according to the selected compatibility matrix. Apply PEP-compliant project normalization only to project lookup within metadata; never mutate the selected OCI repository value.
acceptance_criteria: Route tests cover slash/case/normalization behavior, content negotiation, disabled paths, and prove project lookup cannot select another OCI repository.

title: Serve PyPI Simple API discovery from OCI metadata
description: As a pip user, I can query the configured PyPI endpoints and receive standards-compatible project discovery generated from OCI-backed artifact metadata.
acceptance_criteria: The selected Simple API HTML/JSON representation supports root/project discovery, package links, hashes, requires-python, yanked values, and expected normalization without altering the backing OCI repository name.

title: Implement OCI-backed PyPI package index frontend
description: Provide a standards-compatible PyPI Simple API and distribution downloads backed exclusively by the agreed OCI artifact layout and shared authenticated gateway.
acceptance_criteria: pip can discover and install approved wheel/source artifacts through the proxy using forwarded registry credentials, correct hashes, caching, and safe failure semantics.

title: Validate OCI descriptor length and digest consistency
description: Where the artifact contract supplies immutable descriptors, check supported digest algorithms and advertised lengths before metadata generation or client delivery; define handling for unknown/invalid values.
acceptance_criteria: Tampered descriptor, wrong length, and digest mismatch fixtures fail closed with documented protocol-safe errors.

title: Apply bounded timeout and retry behavior to transport
description: Implement configurable connect/read/write deadlines and retries only for demonstrably safe idempotent retrievals, with cancellation awareness and no retry of uploads or authorization exchanges.
acceptance_criteria: Integration tests cover timeout classes, retry limits/backoff, cancellation, and safe gateway errors; non-idempotent requests never retry.

title: Implement shared credential-safe error response mapping
description: Create typed internal errors and a boundary mapper that preserves intended client/upstream status semantics while redacting URLs, authorization details, and internals.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot tests cover malformed input, upstream failure classes, and unexpected errors, with no secret/credential/upstream-detail leakage.

title: Add health endpoints, graceful shutdown, and redacted logs
description: Provide health/readiness endpoints with no credential or repository data; drain in-flight work on SIGTERM and emit structured logs under the redaction policy.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover ready/not-ready state, shutdown behavior, and ensure health/log output contains no authorization header values.

title: Define credential-safe observability and error policy
description: Specify structured log fields, metric labels, traces, errors, and diagnostic switches that never record authorization data, private repository names when avoidable, signed URLs, or response bodies.
acceptance_criteria: A redaction specification includes positive and negative examples plus automated checks for credentials in logs, telemetry, and error responses.

title: Map OCI failures and HTTP cache semantics to package protocols
description: Define how absent manifests/blobs, invalid layouts, digest mismatches, registry 401/403/404/5xx responses, ETags, Last-Modified, and range behavior are exposed to clients.
acceptance_criteria: The contract maps each upstream class to source-protocol status/body/header behavior without information leakage and records caching requirements per client family.

title: Publish artifact-layout examples and validation fixtures
description: Create small synthetic OCI layouts and expected frontend output examples for the agreed schema so adapters and test fixtures share one source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures validate schema versioning, descriptors, checksums, package metadata, and generated frontend views for each approved ecosystem.

title: Capture representative package-manager HTTP request fixtures
description: Run or collect controlled package-manager interactions for every approved ecosystem to capture request paths, headers, redirects, cache validation, range requests, and expected responses.
acceptance_criteria: Sanitized fixtures contain representative discovery, metadata refresh, archive download, authentication challenge, and missing-object exchanges for each approved protocol.

title: Document release rollout, monitoring, and rollback procedure
description: Specify staged deployment, version pinning, metrics/alerts that do not expose secrets, compatibility communication, rollback to a previous image/config, and OCI artifact-layout upgrade behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A dry run proves rollback can restore the previous release without corrupting clients or changing backing repository names.

title: Write package-client setup and signing guidance
description: Document pip, selected RPM client, apt, and pacman proxy/repository configuration, trusted key setup, authentication behavior, cache updates, and known limitations.
acceptance_criteria: Every command is executed in the e2e suite or marked illustrative; signing/verification requirements and failures are clear for each ecosystem.

title: Write secure deployment and observability guide
description: Document configuration, GHCR scopes/permissions, TLS, upstream allowlisting, resource limits, health checks, container deployment, credential-safe diagnostics, and incident troubleshooting.
acceptance_criteria: A new operator can deploy the fixture-backed example safely and diagnose documented auth/upstream failures without enabling secret logging.

title: Document deployment, artifact publishing, and client configuration
description: As an operator or package consumer, I can publish artifacts to the agreed OCI layout, run the proxy safely, configure each client, understand credentials/signing, and troubleshoot supported failures.
acceptance_criteria: Complete user/operator/developer documentation is validated against test fixtures and accurately lists protocol/version/security boundaries.

title: Set default resource limits and SLO-oriented operational guidance
description: Translate measurements into documented defaults for timeout, header/body limits, concurrency, file descriptors, container resources, and health probes; identify configurable override risks.
acceptance_criteria: Configuration docs list measurement-based defaults and an operator can size/deploy the service using stated resource and availability expectations.

title: Publish generated protocol compatibility test report
description: Collect conformance results in a concise machine-readable and human-readable report showing tested client/version, route, auth mode, signing policy, artifact layout version, and limitations.
acceptance_criteria: CI emits the report and docs link to it; failed/unsupported combinations are clearly distinguished from passing supported ones.

title: Support pip cache validation and metadata error semantics
description: Implement response validators and package-manager-appropriate not-found/invalid-metadata errors according to the common HTTP/error contract.
acceptance_criteria: Conditional requests, cache headers, missing projects, and broken OCI layouts match documented behavior in automated tests.

title: Package service for lean container deployment
description: Supply a minimal multi-stage container build, non-root execution, documented ports/configuration, and a deployment example aligned with the lightweight CPU/memory goal.
acceptance_criteria: A container image builds and starts as non-root, reports health, has a documented configuration example, and contains no build-only tools in the runtime stage.
